In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these residues do not have any significant role in the enzyme function.
neither of the two residues plays a significant role in the catalytic activity of PmGSTB1-1.

, although the N-terminal domain does not appear to play any direct role in the stabilization of glutathione, it is still important for the catalytic activity of the enzyme, possibly by contributing to the binding of glutathione and/or the electrophilic substrate to the active site.
the active-site residues in Beta class GST are not as well conserved as those in the Alpha class GSTs.
the role of the N-terminal domain is not to stabilize glutathione but to stabilize the active site and the C-terminal domain has a more important role in the stabilization of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stabilization of glutathione is not conserved in GSTs and that the origin of this stabilization in the Beta class enzymes remains unknown.

the stabilization of the co-substate glutathione in the active site of PmGSTB1-1 is not achieved by a single residue but by a network of interactions involving both the N- and C-terminal domains of the enzyme.
PmGST B2-2 and other Beta class GSTs are not stabilized by the N-terminal hydroxy-group-containing residue as is the case in other GST classes.
